result.answer:
Verdict: SUPPORTED

Evidence for:
- The paper introduces "a generic modality-attention module which learns to attenuate irrelevant modalities while amplifying the most informative ones to extract contexts from" [S:58b3b70e8883#1] (paper-1802.07862-G50-11-variant.pdf, p.1).
- The paper describes its approach as "adaptive to each sample and token" [S:58b3b70e8883#2] (paper-1802.07862-G50-11-variant.pdf, p.1), indicating token-level adaptation.
- The proposed MNER model with modality attention "significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art text-only NER models" [S:58b3b70e8883#2] (paper-1802.07862-G50-11-variant.pdf, p.1).

Evidence against:
- None in the supplied excerpts. Limitation: the excerpts do not provide ablation or attention-visualization results isolating per-token evidence weighting, nor a detailed textual-vs-visual reweighting mechanism.

citations.title: Multimodal Named Entity Recognition for Short Social Media
citations.text:
We introduce a new task called Multimodal Named Entity Recognition (MNER) for noisy user-generated
data such as tweets or Snapchat captions, which comprise short text with accompanying images. These
social media posts often come in inconsistent or incomplete syntax and lexical notations with very
limited surrounding textual contexts, bringing significant challenges for NER. To this end, we create a
new dataset for MNER called SnapCaptions (Snapchat image-caption pairs submitted to public and
crowd-sourced stories with fully annotated named entities). We then build upon the state-of-the-art
Bi-LSTM word/character based NER models with 1) a deep image network which incorporates relevant
visual context to augment textual information, and 2) a generic modality-attention module which learns
to attenuate irrelevant modalities while amplifying the most informative ones to extract contexts from,

outperforms the state-of-the-art text-only NER models by successfully leveraging provided visual
